session_evidence: Company release 'dLocal to Report Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results' (2026-10-14, carried verbatim on finviz and capital.com): results 'on November 12, 2026 after market close', conference call and video webcast 'November 12, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. Eastern Time'. So the print is after the 11-12 close; the amc window 2026-11-12 close to 2026-11-13 close is correct. https://finviz.com/news/402382/dlocal-to-report-third-quarter-2026-financial-results ; https://capital.com/en-gb/news/dlocal-to-report-third-quarter-2026-financial-results
conviction_note: The print turns on operating profit: the maintained FY26 OP guide (+27.5-32.5% on a ~$220M base) needs H2 OP of $163.6-174.6M against H1's $116.9M and Q2's $64.2M, and consensus EPS of $0.22-0.23 already bakes most of that ramp into Q3, so the asymmetric risk is a light Q3 OP or a trimmed OP guide on a name that sold its last two prints (-13.0%, -4.0%); a moderately crowded short (16.5M shares, 6.3 days) and an easy gross-profit guide hold p_up at 44 rather than lower. The findings sum to -1.6 and the scaled number is -1.32; they agree in sign and size.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus EPS $0.22 (Benzinga https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DLO/earnings-forecasts ; Earnings Whispers https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/DLO) to $0.23 (Chartmill https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/DLO/estimates), revenue $405.9M (Benzinga) to $411.9M (Chartmill): two sources roughly agree, three analysts per Zacks-style data. Company guide is annual only: FY26 TPV +60-70%, gross profit +25-30%, operating profit +27.5-32.5% (6-K ex-99.1, 2026-08-13, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001846832/000184683226000031/ex_991-dlocalxearningsxres.htm), on a FY25 base of TPV $40.8B, GP $403M, OP ~$220M. print_vs_bar_pct is on revenue: the TPV guide implies Q3 TPV ~$16.8-18.8B and revenue/TPV ~2.2-2.3%, so revenue ~$396-415M, in line to slightly above consensus; Q2 beat revenue consensus by ~8% ($399.7M vs $368.9M).
positioning_check: FINRA short interest 16,520,946 shares at the 2026-10-30 settlement (down 864k from 17,385,034 on 10-15), days to cover 6.28 on 2.63M ADV; 5.8% of 286.5M shares outstanding, roughly 12% of the ~135M Class A shares not held by General Atlantic (my estimate from the 13D/A share count) (https://equibles.com/stocks/dlo/short-interest, read 2026-11-12). Short has been easing from 18.2M in mid-August. Options: 25d skew +1.83 vol points (mild put bid, agrees with a negative lean), put/call OI 0.24 (call-heavy), event-implied move 10.72%, priced_direction_lean 'balanced' (sealed baseline). Run-up -8.68% over 20 days and 5 days +2.76%; 12.6% below the 52-week high.

findings.finding: The FY26 operating-profit guide dLocal maintained on 2026-08-13 (+27.5-32.5% YoY on ~$220M = $280.5-291.5M) requires H2 2026 OP of $163.6-174.6M against H1 2026 OP of $116.9M (6-K), i.e. ~$82-87M a quarter against Q2's $64.2M (+15% YoY) and +38-48% over H2 2025's $118.3M (Q3'25 $55.6M + Q4'25 $62.7M); OP/GP must rise from 50% in Q2 to roughly 60-65% in H2 while the GP guide needs only ~$129-139M a quarter against Q2's $127.2M. Consensus EPS $0.22-0.23 (net income ~$67-70M on ~304M diluted shares) already assumes Q3 OP near $78-82M, so the bar embeds the ramp and the plausible miss is OP, or a trimmed OP guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-13): TPV and GP guides raised, OP guide only held, take rate down: -4.0% close-to-close. Q1 2026 (2026-05-14): -13.03%. Q3 2025 (2025-11-12): -6.8% on a revenue beat with margin concerns. Q4 2025 (2026-03-18, first 2026 guide): +9.43%. Sealed baseline history; the other four rows in it are non-earnings 6-Ks (class-action dismissal 04-20, AGM notice 11-04).
findings.why_not_priced: The guide arithmetic is public and one write-up noted the H2 needed to be 'considerably stronger' (marketbeat, 2026-08-13), so this is partly priced: the stock is -8.7% over 20 days. But consensus EPS of $0.22-0.23 sits about 20-25% above Q2's $0.18, i.e. analysts have modelled the ramp rather than doubted it. If the market had priced a likely OP cut, consensus would sit nearer $0.19-0.20 and the skew would be steeper than +1.83.
findings.independence: Q4 2025 OP $62.7M and the original guide base from the Q4 release coverage (https://www.streetinsider.com/Earnings/DLocal+Limited+%28DLO%29+Reports+In-Line+Q4+EPS/26184853.html); Q3 2025 OP $55.6M (https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/dlocal-reports-record-growth-in-q3-2025). Management's own stated mitigants (automation, no material headcount adds in H2; Q1 $4.4M prior-year tax item; FX) are reported in the Q2 call write-up (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/dlocal-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-13/) and argue the ramp is partly mechanical, which is why the size is held at -2.0 and not larger.

findings.finding: Take rate keeps compressing as volume beats: Q2 GP/TPV was 0.72% (from 0.84% in Q1 and 1.07% a year earlier) on a large ride-hailing merchant's ramp and local-to-local at 61% of TPV, and on 2026-09-11 (Goldman Communacopia, mid-Q3) management said TPV growth was over 90% YoY, high-60s excluding the largest merchant, with lower-take-rate verticals (ride-hailing, e-commerce, remittance) driving growth and volume discounts for large merchants. Q3 is therefore likely another TPV/revenue beat against a $406-412M revenue bar with a lower take rate, a mix this stock has sold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue beat by ~8% and TPV +92%, take rate down 12bp QoQ: -4.0%. Q1 2026: take-rate fall, -13.0%. Q3 2025: revenue +52% beat, margin compression: -6.8%. The name has not paid for volume beats that come with take-rate compression.
findings.why_not_priced: Take-rate compression is well known, so this is mostly priced; what is not in the revenue consensus is the volume: a $406-412M bar is only +2-3% over Q2 while management said mid-quarter TPV was still growing >90%. If the market priced the volume, the revenue bar would be higher; if it priced the take-rate fall as harmless, the stock would not have fallen on the last two prints.
findings.independence: Q2 take-rate figures from the 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001846832/000184683226000031/ex_991-dlocalxearningsxres.htm). Peer volume read: MercadoLibre Q3 2026 acquiring TPV +40% FX-neutral (https://www.riotimesonline.com/mercadolibre-earns-us448-million-q3-2026/). Revenue beat and take-rate compression are one fact (the ride-hailing ramp) seen two ways, so they are merged here into one net finding.

findings.finding: Argentine cross-border e-commerce slowed sharply in Q3 after Decree 604/2026 (in force 2026-07-17) changed the courier/postal regime: INDEC courier and postal imports were $960M Jan-Sep 2026 (+59.5% YoY) against $751M Jan-Jul (+83.9%), so Aug+Sep was ~$209M against ~$194M a year earlier, about +8% YoY, with August ($104M) below July ($108M). Argentina is one of dLocal's two largest gross-profit countries and Shein/Temu/Amazon-type cross-border flows carry its higher take rates.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print isolated Argentina cross-border; the Q2 release said Argentina GP growth was broad-based across e-commerce, ride-hailing and delivery with lower advancement costs.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (August INDEC data; Jan-Sep figure from El Economista 2026-11-04)
findings.why_not_priced: It is a Spanish-language Argentine customs series no US preview cites; if it were priced, previews would flag Argentine cross-border as a Q3 drag. It is a proxy: dLocal's Argentina business is mostly local-to-local, and the rest of the company (Brazil GP doubling, ride-hailing) is far larger, so the size is small and net of that.
findings.independence: Jan-Jul figure: https://www.iproup.com/economia-digital/71088-los-argentinos-ya-gastaron-millones-en-shein-temu-y-amazon-este-ano.amp ; Jan-Sep figure: https://eleconomista.com.ar/economia/las-importaciones-via-courier-vuelan-cuales-son-desafios-logisticos-llegar-cuanto-antes-octavo-pais-mas-grande-mundo-n99479 . A proxy, not confirmed by the company or a counterparty.

findings.finding: Short interest is meaningful and easing into the print: 16.5M shares at the 2026-10-30 settlement (5.8% of shares outstanding, ~12% of the non-GA Class A float by my estimate), 6.3 days to cover, down from 18.2M in mid-August; option open interest is call-heavy (put/call 0.24). A clean OP print or a held guide would have a covering mechanism behind it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 print, the one with a guide that surprised up, moved +9.43%; no squeeze-specific history found.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is a mechanism rather than information; it is filed so the squeeze risk against the negative OP thesis is explicit. The fall in short interest (-864k in the last fortnight) suggests some covering already happened, which is why it is small.
findings.independence: FINRA 10-15 settlement 17,385,034 shares, 9.96 days (search result citing FINRA); sealed baseline put/call OI 0.24.

findings.finding: Capital return capacity is large relative to the cap: under the $300M buyback authorised in March 2026 dLocal had used $86.1M (6.9M shares) through 2026-06-30, leaving ~$214M (~5% of a ~$3.95B market cap at $13.79), with $369.1M of corporate cash and a new $150M unsecured credit facility signed 2026-08-12 for general corporate purposes; Q2 dividends paid were $57.2M. Asked what the facility buys: the company is cash-generative and profitable, so it reads as capital-return or working-capital capacity, not distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The buyback authorisation came with the Q4 2025 print (+9.43%); no isolated reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Known capacity; what is not known is whether Q3 repurchases absorbed General Atlantic's August sale at $13.60 or whether a new dividend or accelerated buyback comes with the print. Small because it is an existing programme.
findings.independence: Same document as the guidance finding (the Q2 6-K); counted once here for the capital-return line only.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 FX was benign against prior quarters' headwinds that management used to explain holding the OP guide: the Argentine peso fell ~2.4% and the Brazilian real ~0.3% over Q3 2026, and the Nigerian naira appreciated 0.45% in September (N1,335.50 to N1,329.50).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: management cited FX headwinds versus plan for holding the OP guide; stock -4.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: Currency moves are public; the point is that the FX excuse for H1 OP shortfall did not recur in Q3, which reduces one route to a guide cut. Macro-to-company transmission, small.
findings.independence: LatAm Q3 figures from one Spanish-language roundup (https://ecosistemastartup.com/peso-chileno-lidera-caidas-de-latam-en-3t-2026-protege-tu-startup/), unverified methodology; Egypt not found.

findings.finding: Peer prints since dLocal last spoke show strong emerging-market and payments volume: MercadoLibre Q3 2026 (2026-11-04) acquiring TPV +40% FX-neutral and revenue +45%; Uber Q3 2026 gross bookings +20% cc, mobility +17% cc (ride-hailing is dLocal's largest growth driver) though with a tepid Q4 guide; Adyen Q3 2026 net revenue +23%, Platforms +46%, with its medium-term margin objective withdrawn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: DLO rose +5.46% on 2026-11-04, the day of MercadoLibre's print (no dLocal earnings that day; its 6-K was an AGM notice), so the peer read may already be in the price.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the +5.46% on 11-04 looks like the sympathy move. Filed small because volume is not what has decided this name's prints; take rate and OP are.
findings.independence: Uber: https://investingnews.com/uber-announces-results-for-third-quarter-2026/ ; Adyen: https://www.adyen.com/press-and-media/adyen-publishes-q3-2026-business-update-6r9vz0 . Industry proxies, not dLocal's own numbers.

findings.finding: Brazil's central bank Resolution 561 barred stablecoin/virtual-asset settlement inside regulated eFX cross-border rails from 2026-10-01; dLocal is a licensed Brazilian payments institution with eFX-type cross-border flows, so Q4 commentary may carry a cost or process note, though coverage names Wise, Nomad and Braza Bank and not dLocal.
findings.why_not_priced: Published in May, so public; whether it touches dLocal at all is unknown. Proxy-level, filed small.
findings.independence: https://cointelegraph.com/news/brazil-central-bank-bars-virtual-assets-from-cross-border-payment-service-efx . No document links it to dLocal.

baseline_tension: The negative OP-guide lean agrees with the mild positive skew (+1.83) and the -8.7% 20-day run-up, so part of it is likely priced; it cuts against call-heavy open interest and a short base of 6.3 days, which is why p_up sits at 44 and not lower.
lessons_applied: Lessons 1 and 3: the draft carried a +0.8 revenue/TPV-beat finding and a -1.0 take-rate finding resting on one fact (the ride-hailing ramp); merged them into one reported_quarter finding at -0.5, because this name has sold volume beats that come with take-rate compression
Lessons 5 and 9: Argentina courier-import proxy cut from -0.4 to -0.3, net of dLocal's mostly local-to-local Argentina business and the much larger Brazil and ride-hailing growth
Lesson 7: short interest was already looked up and filed as its own +0.5 positioning finding, so the guidance negative was not shrunk a second time
Lesson 6: bar sourced to two roughly agreeing estimate sources plus the company's annual guide; no cap needed. GA overhang kept in outside_window

Lesson on FPI reaction history: rebuilt the base rate from the four confirmed prints (median abs ~8.1%), which supports abs_move_pct at 11 rather than the baseline's 4.73% median; abs_move_pct and p_up unchanged from the draft
